name: newman-mu
statement: For a Newman polynomial f(z) = sum_{a in A} z^a with A a set of n non-negative integers (coefficients 0/1), let M(A) = min over |z|=1 of |f(z)|. A HIT is an n-term A whose certified lower bound on M(A)^2 strictly exceeds bar(n)^2, where bar(n) is the largest certified M over every envelope member with FEWER than n terms — i.e. a Newman polynomial that beats everything achievable with fewer terms. THE ENVELOPE has two parts, both stored as witness exponent sets and both re-certified at load so no value is ever transcribed (C50): ANCHORS, taken from the literature and the sin-mfg lab records, and ADOPTED, objects this lab certified and then explicitly promoted in a dated edit naming the run and certificate that produced them. The envelope is FROZEN at module load, so a candidate verdict never depends on when it was proposed and a kill-and-resume replays byte-identical; it never absorbs the board automatically. envelopeAudit() reports, without refusing anything, every term count where the board holds a certified value the envelope does not, so an unadopted excess cannot sit unnoticed. The certificate is an exact enclosure of the global minimum of |f|^2 = n + 2*sum_{i<j} cos((a_j-a_i)theta), reduced via cos(d*theta) = T_d(cos theta) to a global minimum of an integer-coefficient polynomial on [-1,1] and certified by Sturm isolation plus interval-Newton refinement with exact rational value enclosures (instruments/trigmin). A separate TRIPWIRE flags any certified M >= 2 carried by at most 18 terms, which would improve the certified record that the least n with mu(n) >= 2 is at most 19; a tripwire is a flag for the owner and is never a result.
